title: Disruptive innovation
author: Wikipedia contributors
paragraphs: In business theory, disruptive innovation is innovation that creates a new market and value network or enters at the bottom of an existing market and eventually displaces established market-leading firms, products, and alliances. In theory, disruptive innovation makes it hard for leading firms to stay at the top of their industry. The term, "disruptive innovation" was popularized by the American academic Clayton Christensen and his collaborators beginning in 1995.

Not all innovations are disruptive, even if they are revolutionary. For example, the first automobiles in the late 19th century were not a disruptive innovation, because early automobiles were expensive luxury items that did not disrupt the market for horse-drawn vehicles. However, the mass-produced automobile was a disruptive innovation, because it changed the transportation market, whereas the first thirty years of automobiles did not.

Disruptive innovations tend to be produced by outsiders and entrepreneurs in startups, rather than existing market-leading companies. The business environment of market leaders does not allow them to pursue disruptive innovations when they first arise, because they are not profitable enough at first and because their development can take scarce resources away from sustaining innovations (which are needed to compete against current competition). Small teams are more likely to create disruptive innovations than large teams. A disruptive process can take longer to develop than by the conventional approach and the risk associated with it is higher than the other more incremental, architectural or evolutionary forms of innovations, but once it is deployed in the market, it achieves a much faster penetration and higher degree of impact on the established markets.

sentence.text: Not all innovations are disruptive, even if they are revolutionary.
sentence.translation: 并非所有创新都具有颠覆性，即使它们具有革命性。
sentence.analysis: Not all 是部分否定，表示“并非所有”，不能理解为“所有……都不”。主句的系表结构是 innovations are disruptive；even if 引导让步条件状语从句，强调“即使具有革命性”也不必然属于文中所定义的颠覆性创新。they 指 innovations。

questions.prompt: 第二段为什么认为最早的汽车不属于颠覆性创新？
options: 它们完全没有采用新技术
它们一开始就已大量生产并改变运输市场
它们价格昂贵，尚未颠覆马车市场
它们出现得比马车更早
questions.explanation: 第二段说最初的汽车是昂贵的奢侈品，没有扰乱马车市场；后来大规模生产的汽车才改变运输市场。
hints: 区分原因与结果，不要把相关现象直接当作因果。
回到第 2 段，逐项核对主体、范围及表示条件或程度的词。

questions.prompt: 第三段给出的、市场领先企业早期不愿推进颠覆性创新的原因是什么？
options: 这类创新在初期必然比现有产品更赚钱
它们从不需要资金或人力资源
初期利润不足，而且可能挤占维持现有竞争力所需的稀缺资源
只有大型团队才能开展这类创新
questions.explanation: 第三段用两个 because 说明初期利润不够，以及开发可能从 sustaining innovations 抽走稀缺资源；并未说颠覆性创新最终不会成功。
